fields.h1: Build Returns Automation That Applies Your Policy to Every Return
fields.hero_description: Build returns automation that sorts each request by your return policy and keeps every return in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for Each Return
fields.features_subheading: Each part runs one stage of a return, and all of them write to the same return record.
fields.feature_1:
Your return policy, applied to every request

Write the return window, the final-sale items, and any exceptions in plain English. The app tests each request against those rules before a label goes out and saves the result.
fields.feature_2:
Exchange or credit offered before a refund

The return portal offers a different size or store credit before it offers money back. You choose the products that qualify and the bonus added to credit, and each pick is recorded.
fields.feature_3:
Return labels from your carrier account

Connect your store platform and your shipping carrier through their APIs. The app creates the return label, follows the tracking scans, and marks the order when the box heads back.
fields.feature_4:
A grade and a photo for every returned item

Staff at the dock pick a grade for each item on a phone or tablet and add a photo when it is damaged. The grade sets the item's next stop: a stock bin, an outlet shelf, or a person.
fields.feature_5:
Return reasons counted by product

Customers pick a reason with each return, and the dashboard counts reasons by product as they arrive. If a product passes a threshold you set, its merchandiser gets a Slack alert.
fields.feature_6:
The returns app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the returns app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Engineers can read how each refund decision is recorded and extend the app like any other codebase.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Stops on a Return's Way Back
fields.tab_content_1:
Within 30 days of delivery, the label goes out

Cobblefen Outdoor takes returns within 30 days of delivery. This week brought 64 requests, and the app checked each delivery date and final-sale flag. A return label went by email to the 58 that passed. The other 6 went to Ysolde Harrowby on support: 4 past 30 days and 2 final-sale items.
fields.tab_content_2:
Size 9.5 ships on the carrier's first scan

Imelda Quarrington starts a return of trail boots in size 9 from Larkmoor Footwear order #31876. The portal offers size 9.5 or store credit of $158 first, then a $148 refund. The credit is the $148 price plus a $10 bonus. She picks size 9.5, and the exchange order ships when the carrier first scans her return.
fields.tab_content_3:
The lamp with a cracked base goes to review

At Brindlewood Home's receiving dock, items graded A go back to stock. Items graded C need a photo and go to Nerys Ramsden, the returns lead, for review. Casimir Vantongeren grades return #4471, which holds 3 items: a throw and a vase pass as grade A. The table lamp has a cracked base and is graded C.
fields.tab_content_4:
26 of 40 jacket returns say it runs small

Ferncastle Apparel's Monday report counts return reasons by product. Last month the Harbor rain jacket came back 40 times: 26 said it runs small, 9 changed their minds, and 5 arrived damaged. When one reason covers more than half of a product's returns, Philippa Okwuosa, the merchandiser, gets a direct message.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn your return policy into returns automation with clear rules and grades, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write your return policy as rules
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose what shows before a refund
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Connect the systems around a return
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write your return policy down as rules a machine can test: the window in days from delivery, which items are final sale, and the condition an item must arrive in. Mark each rule as automatic or as one that sends the request to a person.
fields.howto_step_2_des: For every outcome, name the action and the owner. An approved request gets a label by email, a declined one gets the reason in writing, and an exception lands in the support queue. Keep the list short enough to learn in one read.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what the portal shows before money back. Offer exchanges only on sizes in stock, and try a small credit bonus, such as $10, on one product line for a month before you extend it to the rest of the catalog.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the store platform that holds your orders, the carrier that prints return labels, and the payment system that issues refunds, each through its API. Describe the flow in a prompt, and Emergent builds the portal and the rules on top.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Define grades for the receiving dock
fields.howto_step_5_des: Agree on 2 or 3 grades that receiving staff can apply without a manual, and give each grade one next stop. Require a photo for any grade that holds up a refund, and name the person who reviews those photos.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pull 20 returns from last month, including a late request, a final-sale item, and a damaged one. Run them through the app and check that each gets the outcome it got by hand. Fix any rule by prompting, then run the set again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live on one product line
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn on the portal for one product line first, such as footwear, and watch the support queue for a week. Read the first monthly reasons report before you add the next line, and move the rest over once the queue stays small.

faq_plan.a: Returns automation is software that runs each product return by rules you set. It checks the request against your policy, sends the return label, offers an exchange or credit, records the grade when the item arrives, and logs the refund. People see only the requests the rules send them.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up returns automation?
faq_plan.a: Start from your written return policy and turn each line into a rule: the return window and who reviews the exceptions. Then decide what the portal offers before a refund and how the dock grades items. In Emergent's AI automation builder, you describe those rules in plain English and get a working returns app with its database.

faq_plan.q: How do online stores choose returns automation software?
faq_plan.ref: how online stores choose returns automation software
faq_plan.a: Run your own return policy through each option instead of watching a demo. Check that it reads orders from your store platform, prints labels with your carrier, handles exchanges as well as refunds, and lets you query the return data. Price it at your busiest month's volume. Emergent builds the returns app from a prompt, and each return lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I use returns automation to upsell customers during a return?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation platforms upsell customers during returns
faq_plan.a: Set the return portal to show an exchange or store credit before the refund, and place a matching product next to the credit offer. Credit with a small bonus gives the customer a reason to stay, and the product beside it gives them something to spend it on. Keep the sizes customers swap into in stock by reordering them through procurement automation.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up fraud checks in returns automation?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation software prevents fraudulent returns
faq_plan.a: Write each check as a rule that compares the return with its order and holds the refund on a mismatch. Useful rules cover an item that was never on the order, a request outside the window, and a received SKU that differs from the one shipped. Add a limit on returns per customer in 90 days. A held refund waits for a person to decide; the flag itself accuses no one.

faq_plan.q: What are the benefits of returns automation as order volume grows?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation can help your business grow
faq_plan.a: The main benefit is that the returns workload stops growing at the pace of orders. Rules approve every request inside the policy and send the label without anyone typing. Staff handle only the exceptions, and the hours support spent on routine returns can go to customers who have not bought yet. Automations built with Emergent have no task cap.

faq_plan.q: How can I use returns automation data to cut future returns?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation can lead to long-term growth
faq_plan.a: Count returns by product and reason every month, then fix the cause behind the biggest count. Look for a size chart, a product photo, or a supplier behind it. After the fix, next month's count shows whether returns of that product fell. Returns are one part of ecommerce automation, and the same order record can feed both.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect photos for item verification in returns automation?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation systems handle image uploads for item verification
faq_plan.a: Ask for a photo in two places: on the return request and at the receiving dock. The customer uploads one with a damage claim, and receiving staff take their own when they grade the item. A person compares the two before approving the claim. In an app built with Emergent, every photo stays with its return record in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I calculate and track cost savings from returns automation?
faq_plan.ref: how to calculate total cost savings from returns automation
faq_plan.a: Add three monthly figures, subtract the software's running cost, and track the result against the month before you switched. First, minutes saved per return times returns handled, times the hourly cost of the person who handled them. Second, the value of refunds that became exchanges or store credit. Third, the value of items restocked sooner after grading.

faq_plan.q: What is the best way to speed up warehouse receiving with returns automation?
faq_plan.ref: how returns automation improves warehouse efficiency
faq_plan.a: Link every return label to a record of its items and reason: receiving then knows what is in each box before anyone opens it. Send restockable items straight to a bin instead of a holding pile. Return items graded defective to the supplier for a credit, and let accounts payable automation match that credit against the next bill.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Returns Automation That Applies Your Policy to Every Return', meta title 'Returns Automation From Request to Restock | Emergent' and hero 'Build returns automation that sorts each request by your return policy and keeps every return in a database you own.' (116 chars, carries the primary, leads with Build) cover the whole job; howto_description 'Seven steps to turn your return policy into returns automation with clear rules and grades, then build it with Emergent.' is one sentence, 120 chars. No sibling topic (shipping, order processing) in the H1.

intent.evidence: Top 10 are returns vendors' explainers and tool lists (ReturnLogic, nShift, ReverseLogix, Outvio, Loop). The page gives the definition (FAQ 1), how to choose software (FAQ 3), a 7-step how-to specific to returns ('01 Write your return policy as rules', '05 Define grades for the receiving dock', '06 Test with last month's returns'), fraud checks, photo verification and a savings formula. The comparison table compares general automation platforms, not the returns tools in the SERP (note).

specificity.evidence: Returns vocabulary throughout: 'the return window, the final-sale items, and any exceptions', 'store credit of $158 ... the $148 price plus a $10 bonus', 'ships when the carrier first scans her return', 'items graded A go back to stock', 'a received SKU that differs from the one shipped', 'a stock bin, an outlet shelf, or a person'. No hub boilerplate; table built by the skeleton from the library.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on full sentences with verbs: 'Write the return window', 'The return portal offers', 'Connect your store platform', 'Staff at the dock pick a grade', 'Customers pick a reason', 'Export the full code'. Tabs open on the company or person: 'Cobblefen Outdoor takes returns within 30 days', 'Imelda Quarrington starts a return', 'At Brindlewood Home's receiving dock', 'Ferncastle Apparel's Monday report'.

craft.evidence: Sentences carry one idea and end on the key word ('A flag holds the refund; it does not accuse anyone.'); QC Q5 and Q2 clean at P0/P1. Triplet count, the FAQ 2 colon list and the FAQ 9 formula logic recorded as notes.

voice.evidence: Calm, product-led, concrete: 'The other 6 went to Ysolde Harrowby on support: 4 past 30 days and 2 final-sale items.'; 'Pull 20 returns from last month, including a late request, a final-sale item, and a damaged one.' No hype, no AI-tell vocabulary. FAQ 7's echo opener and the features_subheading frame recorded as notes.

truth.evidence: Every Emergent sentence maps to claims_used: 'from a prompt' (prompt-build), 'a database you own' (database-owned), 'through their APIs' (api-connect), 'gets a Slack alert' (alerts), 'the dashboard counts reasons by product as they arrive' (realtime), 'Export the full code ... on paid plans' (code-export), 'with no cap on tasks' (no-caps); all seven ids are approved in rules/capabilities.json. No sentence claims a step stops or prevents a risk (FAQ 5: 'A flag holds the refund; it does not accuse anyone.'). No third-party statistic, law or named-vendor fact in prose. Numbers agree in copy, mockup and images: 58+4+2=64, 4+2=6, 148+10=158, 26+9+5=40, 3 items in #4471. Unsourced category-practice sentences (FAQ 4, 5, 8, 10) and FAQ 10's 'what is in each box' recorded as notes.

distinct.evidence: Reads as its own page: four returns stages (policy check, exchange first, dock grading, reasons by product) that no ecommerce-cluster sibling covers (ecommerce, shipping, order-processing, procurement and AP specs carry no returns copy). The how-to's '06 Test with last month's returns' shape is shared with two siblings (note).

Hub link in item 2; sibling links in 4, 7, 10. Emergent moat lines in items 3 and 8, and neither answer names another company. PA6-flagged slots 4-10 wait for Divit's packet. findings.issue: None of the three ranks in this page's top 10 (QC K7 P2). The SERP is returns tools and their guides (ReturnLogic, Loop Returns, Outvio, ReverseLogix, nShift); a buyer comparing returns software sees none of them. The Auto library has no returns-management category, so the skeleton fell back to general automation platforms, as on customer-service-automation, audit-workflow and invoice-approval-workflow.
findings.fix: Coordinator adds a returns-management category (Loop Returns, ReturnLogic, AfterShip Returns) to rules/competitors with sourced facts; the skeleton then picks from it.

findings.quote: They upsell by showing an exchange or store credit before the refund.
findings.issue: Four FAQ sentences describe what returns platforms or AP automation do as a class, with no domain_sources entry and plan.claims_to_source empty: item 4 'They upsell by showing an exchange or store credit before the refund.'; item 5 'It compares each return with its order and flags the ones that do not match, for a person to decide.'; item 8 'They attach each photo to the return and the item it shows.'; item 10 'Items graded defective can go back to the supplier for a credit, which accounts payable automation then matches against the next bill.' Each names no third party and matches common practice (exchange-first and bonus-credit flows are the subject of the Loop Returns article in the top 10), so this is a note, as A-r-9 ruled for a category definition. Item 4 also calls a same-price size swap an upsell; the true upsell is the third sentence ('show a matching product next to the credit offer').
findings.fix: List category-practice statements in plan.claims_to_source and quote a span for each, or phrase them as what the reader's app does ('Show an exchange or store credit before the refund').

findings.quote: It tells receiving what is in each box before anyone opens it, because the return label links to a record of the items and the reason.
findings.issue: The record holds what the customer said they are sending, not what the box holds. The page's own FAQ 5 lists 'a received SKU that differs from the one shipped' as a check, so a careful reader sees the two answers pull against each other. Read as 'what to expect' it is fine for an ops reader, so it ships as a note.
findings.fix: It tells receiving what each box should hold before anyone opens it, because the return label links to a record of the items and the reason.

findings.quote: Keep the sizes customers swap into in stock by reordering them through procurement automation.
findings.issue: Both linking sentences send the reader to pages that do not cover what the sentence promises. Item 4: the procurement-automation spec covers purchase requests, supplier quotes and catalog buying, with no stock reordering; the sentence also leaves the upsell question to place the link. Item 10: 'which accounts payable automation then matches against the next bill' links to a page about invoice-to-PO matching and payment runs that never mentions supplier credits.
findings.fix: Item 4: link automated inventory management once it is live, or move the procurement link to a sentence about buying. Item 10: keep the link on a sentence the AP page covers (matching supplier bills).

findings.quote: Within 30 days of delivery → label by email
findings.issue: Tab 1 states half the rule in three places: the drawn prompt 'Email a label for returns inside 30 days, and send the rest to support', the rule banner 'Within 30 days of delivery → label by email', and the tab H3 'Within 30 days of delivery, the label goes out'. The tab's own 2 final-sale requests fall inside the window and still go to support. Copy and image agree on every number and outcome, and the drawn note 'Checked: delivery date, final-sale flag' carries the second check, so this does not contradict the copy.
findings.fix: Prompt 'Email a label for returns inside 30 days that are not final sale, and send the rest to support'; banner 'Within 30 days, not final sale → label by email'.

findings.issue: The shipped exchange-order panel carries a 'Credit offer' row for a credit Imelda did not take. It is there to show the 148 + 10 = 158 check, but it reads as part of the shipped order.
findings.fix: Move the '$148 + $10 bonus' breakdown under 'Store credit $158' on the phone screen and give the panel an order-only row (for example the return it replaces).

findings.quote: the dashboard counts reasons by product as they arrive
findings.issue: The reasons report has three cadences on one page: feature_5 'counts reasons by product as they arrive' with 'a Slack alert'; tab_content_4 'Ferncastle Apparel's Monday report' that counts 'Last month'; howto_step_7_des 'Read the first monthly reasons report'; FAQ 7 'a monthly count'. A weekly report on last month's numbers would also send Philippa the same direct message four Mondays running. Each is buildable, so this is consistency, not a false claim.
findings.fix: Pick one cadence in the copy (a Monday report on the last 30 days) and name it the same way in step 7 and FAQ 7.

findings.quote: Second, refunds that became exchanges or store credit.
findings.issue: Item 9's formula counts retained revenue (and unspent store credit, a liability) as a cost saving, and 'compare the result with the month before you switched' compares a savings figure with a month that had none by definition. Advice, so a note.
findings.fix: Count the margin kept on refunds that became exchanges, and compare this month's handling cost per return with the month before you switched.

review_notes.issue: None of the three ranks in this page's top 10 (QC K7 P2). The SERP is returns tools and their guides (ReturnLogic, Loop Returns, Outvio, ReverseLogix, nShift); a buyer comparing returns software sees none of them. The Auto library has no returns-management category, so the skeleton fell back to general automation platforms, as on customer-service-automation, audit-workflow and invoice-approval-workflow.
review_notes.fix: Coordinator adds a returns-management category (Loop Returns, ReturnLogic, AfterShip Returns) to rules/competitors with sourced facts; the skeleton then picks from it.

review_notes.issue: Four FAQ sentences describe what returns platforms or AP automation do as a class, with no domain_sources entry and plan.claims_to_source empty: item 4 'They upsell by showing an exchange or store credit before the refund.'; item 5 'It compares each return with its order and flags the ones that do not match, for a person to decide.'; item 8 'They attach each photo to the return and the item it shows.'; item 10 'Items graded defective can go back to the supplier for a credit, which accounts payable automation then matches against the next bill.' Each names no third party and matches common practice (exchange-first and bonus-credit flows are the subject of the Loop Returns article in the top 10), so this is a note, as A-r-9 ruled for a category definition. Item 4 also calls a same-price size swap an upsell; the true upsell is the third sentence ('show a matching product next to the credit offer').
review_notes.fix: List category-practice statements in plan.claims_to_source and quote a span for each, or phrase them as what the reader's app does ('Show an exchange or store credit before the refund').

review_notes.issue: The record holds what the customer said they are sending, not what the box holds. The page's own FAQ 5 lists 'a received SKU that differs from the one shipped' as a check, so a careful reader sees the two answers pull against each other. Read as 'what to expect' it is fine for an ops reader, so it ships as a note.
review_notes.fix: It tells receiving what each box should hold before anyone opens it, because the return label links to a record of the items and the reason.

review_notes.issue: Both linking sentences send the reader to pages that do not cover what the sentence promises. Item 4: the procurement-automation spec covers purchase requests, supplier quotes and catalog buying, with no stock reordering; the sentence also leaves the upsell question to place the link. Item 10: 'which accounts payable automation then matches against the next bill' links to a page about invoice-to-PO matching and payment runs that never mentions supplier credits.
review_notes.fix: Item 4: link automated inventory management once it is live, or move the procurement link to a sentence about buying. Item 10: keep the link on a sentence the AP page covers (matching supplier bills).

review_notes.issue: Tab 1 states half the rule in three places: the drawn prompt 'Email a label for returns inside 30 days, and send the rest to support', the rule banner 'Within 30 days of delivery → label by email', and the tab H3 'Within 30 days of delivery, the label goes out'. The tab's own 2 final-sale requests fall inside the window and still go to support. Copy and image agree on every number and outcome, and the drawn note 'Checked: delivery date, final-sale flag' carries the second check, so this does not contradict the copy.
review_notes.fix: Prompt 'Email a label for returns inside 30 days that are not final sale, and send the rest to support'; banner 'Within 30 days, not final sale → label by email'.

review_notes.issue: The shipped exchange-order panel carries a 'Credit offer' row for a credit Imelda did not take. It is there to show the 148 + 10 = 158 check, but it reads as part of the shipped order.
review_notes.fix: Move the '$148 + $10 bonus' breakdown under 'Store credit $158' on the phone screen and give the panel an order-only row (for example the return it replaces).

review_notes.issue: The reasons report has three cadences on one page: feature_5 'counts reasons by product as they arrive' with 'a Slack alert'; tab_content_4 'Ferncastle Apparel's Monday report' that counts 'Last month'; howto_step_7_des 'Read the first monthly reasons report'; FAQ 7 'a monthly count'. A weekly report on last month's numbers would also send Philippa the same direct message four Mondays running. Each is buildable, so this is consistency, not a false claim.
review_notes.fix: Pick one cadence in the copy (a Monday report on the last 30 days) and name it the same way in step 7 and FAQ 7.

review_notes.issue: Item 9's formula counts retained revenue (and unspent store credit, a liability) as a cost saving, and 'compare the result with the month before you switched' compares a savings figure with a month that had none by definition. Advice, so a note.
review_notes.fix: Count the margin kept on refunds that became exchanges, and compare this month's handling cost per return with the month before you switched.

review_notes.issue: 15 'A, B, and C' lists read templated (QC Q8 threshold 8): meta_description (4 items); why_description 'the return portal, the dock grading screen, and the reasons report'; feature_1 'the return window, the final-sale items, and any exceptions'; feature_3 'creates the return label, follows the tracking scans, and marks the order'; feature_4 'a stock bin, an outlet shelf, or a person'; tab_content_4 '26 said ..., 9 ..., and 5 ...'; howto_step_1_des 'the window ..., which items ..., and the condition'; howto_step_2_des 'An approved request ..., a declined one ..., and an exception'; howto_step_4_des 'the store platform ..., the carrier ..., and the payment system'; howto_step_6_des 'a late request, a final-sale item, and a damaged one'; FAQ 1 (5 items); FAQ 3 (4 items); FAQ 5 'an item ..., a request ..., or a received SKU'; FAQ 7 'size charts, photos, or suppliers'; FAQ 9 'First ... Second ... Third'.
review_notes.fix: Break three or four of them into two sentences or pairs; keep the ones that are data.
